title: Choose the visual world for Vasanam
question: The roll assigned Release-Night Banner Street, translated into your black-and-green brief. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Release-Night Banner Street
options.lineage: Hand-painted Kollywood release banners on bamboo scaffolding, floodlit at night
options.thesis: Every upload gets a release-night title board: Tamil above, English below, painted big and lit against the dark.
options.viewport: A black night street; one giant green board stands at depth on scaffolding, its Tamil and English lines painting on in sync with a playing clip, the Start free plaque nailed to the board.
options.risk: Banner culture tips into fan-cutout kitsch if the lettering discipline slips; it must read as a working page, not a poster.

raised.raise: Two-enamel rule: every board uses at most two paints plus black; no gradients, no glows.
Addressable reel: each section carries a real timecode address that doubles as the header navigation.
Scale is hierarchy: one painted word per board is biggest, and it is the one that matters.
Label strip: every plan and feature board carries the same small painted label strip (name, minutes, price).
One light governs: a single warm floodlight temperature lights every board; nothing glows on its own.

options.label: Censor Certificate
options.lineage: The CBFC certificate frame that opens every Tamil film
options.thesis: The page opens like a film: a certified title frame, bilingual and official, then the reel rolls.
options.viewport: A full black frame holding one ornate bordered certificate card naming the clip, its Tamil and English subtitle lines, runtime, and a Start free stamp.
options.risk: The certificate is the most familiar frame in Tamil cinema; it can read as a costume if the card stops being a working form.

options.label: Session Sleeve
options.thesis: Each cut as a record sleeve: a hard-cropped duotone still and one flat green band carrying the subtitle line.
options.viewport: A duotone still cropped hard into a corner, a full-strength green band across the rest, the Tamil line set big across it at an angle.
options.case: Holds clarity: the band is a strong frame for subtitle lines. Loses identification: jazz sleeves are not this audience's world, and it needs real film stills you do not have yet.
options.risk: Without real stills the crop has nothing to hold.

options.label: Risograph Print
options.viewport: Ink-layered sections on a paper ground.
options.risk: Light paper ground breaks the dark brief.
options.case: Loses both axes: not the editor's world, and a light ground contradicts the brief.

options.label: Teletext Magazine
options.thesis: Numbered pages in a fixed character grid.
options.risk: Retro novelty for an Indian audience that never used teletext.
options.case: Loses both: no cultural pull here, and the rigid grid fights Tamil script.

options.label: Punk Paste-up Zine
options.risk: The opposite of the clean, classic brief.
options.case: Loses both: gritty where the brief asks clean, and foreign to the audience.

options.label: Sneaker Box Wall
options.thesis: A wall of labelled boxes you slide open.
options.risk: Orange box board fights the black-and-green brief.
options.case: Loses both: no link to subtitling or editors.
options.kept: One label grid rules every card.

options.label: Indoor Weather Sun
options.viewport: A half sun doubled by a mirror.
options.risk: Amber monochrome breaks the green brief.
options.case: Loses both: atmospheric, but says nothing about subtitles.
options.kept: A single light governs the palette.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark product page in the manner of polished developer tools, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and Start free on the left, a large tilted screenshot of the subtitle editor on the right.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other AI tool's landing page by design.
